text.text: Mulee’aage was built between 1914 and 1919 for Prince Hassan Izzuddeen, and later became the official presidential residence.
Four significant locations. Illustrations by the Malé group.
text.label: Figures

text.text: Hukuru Miskiy, the Old Friday Mosque, was built in the 17th century from finely carved coral stone. It is one of Malé’s most important landmarks.
Sultan Park stands on the grounds of the old royal palace. It marks the change from monarchy to republic, and hosts national celebrations.
Jumhooree Maidhaan, Republic Square, is Malé’s main civic space, used for national ceremonies and public celebrations.
